title: Control-to-requirement mapping
description: Each control is mapped to the framework requirements it satisfies (SOC 2, ISO 27001, internal policy). The mapping shows coverage: which requirements have controls and which do not. Mappings are reviewed when frameworks update. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers mapping controls to requirements.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 4, 2: 8, 3: 12}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
reqs = ["R%d" % i for i in range(N)]
covered = {r: (i % 3 != 2) for i, r in enumerate(reqs)}
gaps = [r for r, c in covered.items() if not c]
print("requirements:", N, "| covered:", sum(covered.values()), "| gaps:", gaps or ["none"])
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Remediation tracking
description: Each violation gets a remediation plan with steps, owner, and due date; closure requires evidence that the fix works, not just that it was attempted. Plans track planned, in-progress, and verified-closed states. Reopened violations link to their history. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers plans with steps, owners, due dates.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: ["planned"], 2: ["planned", "in-progress"], 3: ["planned", "in-progress", "verified-closed"]}
states = CFG[LEVEL]
closed = states[-1] == "verified-closed"
print("remediation:", " -> ".join(states), "| closed:", closed)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Compliance gap analysis
description: Required controls are compared against implemented controls to list gaps: missing, partial, or untested. Each gap gets a risk rating and a remediation owner. Gap analysis runs on schedule and after every framework change. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers required vs implemented comparison.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: (10, 9), 2: (20, 15), 3: (50, 40)}
required, have = CFG[LEVEL]
gaps = required - have
print("required:", required, "| implemented:", have, "| gaps:", gaps)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
